text.text: José Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday. Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappé struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break. Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant. But Madrid scored three goals in the final six minutes, all stemming from corners, to turn the game on its head as Carlos Espí, Endrick and the former Roma defender Antonio Rüdiger struck at a stunned Stadio Olimpico. Mourinho was a popular figure as he led Roma to the Conference League title and Europa League final during two-and-a-half years in charge. The Portuguese coach was honoured with banners and chants by the home crowd in Roma’s first home Champions League match in more than seven years. Pacer Shamar Joseph repeatedly resorted to short-pitched deliveries, peppering Indian batters with bouncers even when the target was well beyond reach. Tailender Arshdeep Singh faced the impact and even got hurt in the process. In the final over, Arshdeep started Shamar's over with a boundary, followed by a wide and a dot. Shamar bowled a bouncer on the third ball, which struck the Indian cricketer on the arm, leaving him in pain. The medical staff attended to Arshdeep, who decided to continue despite being advised to walk off the field. The Windies pacer bowled yet another bouncer, but Arshdeep eventually walked off as India scored 223. Sunil Gavaskar, the legendary Indian cricketer, was not impressed with the visitors' tactics. text.text: Sanju Samson added another milestone to his T20I career on Wednesday, becoming only the sixth Indian batter to hit 100 sixes in the format during the fourth T20I against West Indies at Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium. The wicketkeeper-batter reached the landmark in style while launching India's pursuit of a daunting 248-run target, producing an explosive 56 off just 23 deliveries.Samson's aggressive innings featured six fours and four sixes at a strike rate of 243.48, giving India early momentum after West Indies captain Shai Hope struck an unbeaten century to power the visitors to 247/3. However, Samson's counterattack ended when Keemo Paul dismissed him for 56, with Shimron Hetmyer completing a catch near the boundary.Samson joins India's elite six-hitting clubWith 102 sixes to his name in T20Is, Samson has joined an exclusive group of Indian batters to have crossed the 100-six mark. The former Red Bull chief explained why he chose to start his book here in a discussion with Motorsport.com ahead of the book's 22 October release. A hook using a season worthy of a whole book "I just wanted to grab the reader, you know, page one," Horner said, treating the opening as a storytelling decision rather than something he needed to get off his chest. Then-Mercedes driver Hamilton and Red Bull ace Verstappen arrived at the finale level on points - a rare end to what was an exciting year. Red Bull also went in 28 points behind Mercedes in the constructors' standings. Horner argues the whole thing was beyond fiction: "That season was an epic. text.text: Carlos Alcaraz should stop complaining about scheduling issues and make bold decisions on the tournaments he wants to play. That’s the verdict of former world No 4 Greg Rusedski, who has suggested Alcaraz has more than enough money in his bank to take control of his schedule and skip events he doesn’t want to play. Alcaraz has hinted that he is not a fan of ATP 1000 tournaments that are played over an extended 12-day period and there were suggestions that he was not committing to all his media duties at this week’s Shanghai event in what was seen as a ‘mini protest’. ATP 1000 tournaments are ‘mandatory’ events for the top players and that means they don’t get appearance fees to play, but the story was different last week as Alcaraz would have collected a big guaranteed fee just to play in the Japan Open. That big appearance payment and the prize money he won for winning the title in Tokyo made that a much more lucrative week for Alcaraz than his brief stay in Shanghai, which ended when he lost to Belgium’s Zizous Bergs. The newly formed Six Kings Slam has attracted the top stars in the tennis world in recent years, with a potential $6 million prize pool as a major motivator for players. However, this time around, should the players wish to collect their hefty paychecks, they will need to wait slightly longer given the current situation of the tournament. “Riyadh Season has announced the postponement of the third edition of the international “Six Kings Slam” tennis tournament, originally scheduled for October 21, 22, and 24, to December 27–30, 2026,” was the official statement by the tournament on X [https://x.com/turki_alalshikh/status/2110379174028628422?s=46]. “The decision reflects Riyadh Season’s commitment to delivering sporting events to the highest standards, following an assessment of the organizational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and their potential impact on the quality of the audience experience.” The decision is not a surprise to anyone, given the escalation of military hostilities in the region. text.text: Carlos Alcaraz has won three titles from four finals so far this season. Carlos Alcaraz has repeatedly expressed his displeasure with the packed ATP schedule, often urging the bosses not to "push" the players too much, as it can lead to injuries when they don't get enough time to rest and recover between tournaments. Now it has come to light that he is protesting behind the scenes at tournaments. Alcaraz was last seen in action in the third round of the Shanghai Masters, where Zizou Bergs won 7-5, 7-6(4). The Spaniard complained about inconsistent balls throughout the match. If Alcaraz fails to take home the Paris Masters, also the season's last Masters 1000 event, then he will end the season without winning a title at this level for the first time since 2021. He has played only one Masters 1000 final this season, at the Monte-Carlo Masters, where he lost to his arch-rival Jannik Sinner , who ended his season after defending his Wimbledon title due to a knee injury. text.text: Gael Monfils has officially retired from tennis after 22 years. The flamboyant Frenchman was expected to bring the curtain down on his glittering career at his home tournament at the Paris Masters, but he has already appeared on the ITIA's inactive list in recent days. Monfils had confirmed that he would retire in 2026 after a masterful career that brought him to a career ranking high of world No 6 on the ATP Tour. The Frenchman also claimed 13 career titles and reached, three Masters finals, and three Grand Slam semifinals. Monfils would surely have collected more titles if it were not for the dominance of Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer, and Rafael Nadal, who were all at the peak of their powers at the same time as the Frenchman. He was asked which of the 'big three' were the toughest to play in his career and he was forthright with his answer. text.text: On a night dominated by the apparent status of Kristaps Porzingis, the absence of the Latvian big was felt at times during the Golden State Warriors’ 101-89 win over the Los Angeles Lakers at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. Steve Kerr’s intention to spread the floor in a so-called ‘5-out’ alignment banked on players who are able to space to floor — including their center. Porzingis happens to fit that profile, while also being 7-foot-3-inches. Without Porzingis — and also not having Al Horford available tonight — the Warriors were not only small, they were bereft of shooting and spacing personnel. That was apparent at times during this game, where the Warriors were able to rally back from a significant deficit, albeit during a time when both teams’ main characters’ nights were finished (one of them, Luka Doncic, did not suit up for the Lakers). Once again, it was rookie Yaxel Lendeborg who stood out. He finished with 17 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists in just under 24 minutes of time on the floor. text.text: Former Manchester United striker Wayne Rooney has strongly criticised ex-teammate Cristiano Ronaldo after the veteran forward abandoned the Portugal national team camp during the recent international window. The retired England international questioned how his old Old Trafford colleague handled the public fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus. The former England striker has fiercely condemned his old colleague's decision to abandon the national team camp following a bitter dispute over playing time. That row erupted after the 41-year-old forward was left unused throughout a 2-1 UEFA Nations League victory over Norway despite warming up for 30 minutes. Walking out ahead of the Denmark clash, he released a statement accusing his boss of " breaking his word " while comparing himself to Pele and Diego Maradona. Ironically, the veteran forward had previously won silverware under Jesus at club level with Al-Nassr and even recommended him for the national team post after the 2026 World Cup. However, his decision to issue a public statement apologising to his team-mates while openly attacking his manager was widely viewed as an affront to both the dressing room and the federation.

text.text: McLaren 's Andrea Stella confirmed that the team is "not finished" with its Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri talks, after the pair collided in Singapore. Both MCL40s were sent into synchronised spins when the drivers made contact late in the Sprint around Marina Bay. McLaren is happy to move on from analysing blame in the incident, but wants to achieve a clear, united plan moving forward. The papaya duo, in battle for P6, collided on the final lap of the Singapore Sprint. Both cars went spinning, with Norris only able to get going again. He finished P8. Quick to apologise to the team, the Brit had initially defended his right to go for the gap. After the Grand Prix on Sunday, he shifted that stance to admit the move should never have been attempted at all. Piastri noted his teammate's apology and said they had moved on. Norris even offered to help his younger teammate, who was chasing Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari, in the closing stages of the Grand Prix. It was a welcome sight for team principal Stella, who confirmed that conversations remain ongoing within the Woking squad. Well, in short, there have been years of collaboration to ensure the sport found the best partner to deliver a sustainable, world-class Grand Prix that will stand the test of time for generations to come. “Africa has always been part of Formula 1’s future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way, with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating meaningful impact,” said F1 President and CEO Stefano Domenicali. There had been a lot of interested parties who wanted to bring F1 to Africa but after extensive conversations, a deal was agreed to secure the Formula 1 African Grand Prix, presented by Visit Rwanda.
